description: The webview gets no shell access at all. Sidecars are spawned only from Rust, inside #[tauri::command] handlers, and tauri-plugin-shell's Rust API (Shell::sidecar -> Command::new_sidecar) does not consult this ACL - scope is enforced in the plugin's IPC command handlers, which nothing in this app calls. So granting shell:allow-spawn here would add attack surface without enabling any function: a compromised webview (a malicious track title, a bad frontend dependency) could then spawn yt-dlp with arbitrary argv, and yt-dlp has --exec. dialog:allow-open is the folder picker for local import; the scan itself runs in Rust. core:window:allow-set-title lets the video window name itself after its track - core:default does not include it.
